marketDirection.headline: Indian market is range-bound today.

reasons.text: Nifty 50 closed -1.11% at 22,889, above its 20-DMA, below the 50-DMA (falling), below the 200-DMA.
The index is up 2.4% over the last five sessions — no clear directional edge (range-bound).
Market breadth is defensive — 17.8% of scanned NSE stocks advancing, 20.2% above their 50-DMA.
Contract accretion reinforces earnings visibility, setting up swing support checks near ₹365–₹370 ahead of the October 30 results catalyst.
Daily rejection candle below 23,000 indicates market-wide breakout attempts remain prone to failure; swing traders should tighten stops and reduce position sizing on non-earnings setups.

marketSummary: Indian benchmark indices erased intraday gains on October 21, 2026, with the Nifty 50 closing 77.60 points lower at 22,811.35 and the Sensex declining 143.21 points to 73,709.69. The session was marked by sharp sectoral divergence: ER&D and IT counters rallied following strong Q2 results and heavy AI-led order flow, while cyclical heavyweights, capital goods, and defence baskets came under distribution. Elevated crude oil prices and sustained FII net selling kept swing traders cautious around overhead index resistance at the 23,000–23,200 band.
dailyFocus: Prioritize high-volume post-earnings expansions in IT/ER&D while demanding disciplined confirmation on base pullbacks in Defence and Power Capex names ahead of key Q2 earnings triggers.

sectors.name: Nifty IT & ER&D Services
sectors.reason: Clear relative strength and volume expansion driven by strong Q2 earnings beats, expanding EBIT margins, and robust deal pipelines in Engineering Research & Development and Enterprise AI.
catalysts: Strong Q2 FY27 print and mid-16% EBIT margin delivery by LTTS
Over $200 million quarterly large-deal TCV with AI wins exceeding 50%
Resilient deal booking commentary from tier-1 and mid-tier software exporters
risks: Headwinds in European automotive OEM discretionary spending
Currency fluctuations and elevated US bond yields capping broader tech multiples

sectors.name: Power Capex & Capital Goods
sectors.reason: Multiquarter order backlogs and structural grid expansion provide strong fundamental support, though near-term momentum is consolidating ahead of imminent Q2 FY27 earnings prints.
catalysts: High order-book visibility in transmission, distribution, and industrial electrification
Spillover tailwinds from AI data center power infrastructure demand
Upcoming Q2 financial releases clarifying margin defense amid commodity moves
risks: Intraday profit booking below key short-term moving averages
Execution delay risks in heavy electrical equipment installations

sectors.name: Retail & Consumption
sectors.reason: High-growth fast fashion formats continue to show robust top-line additions, but rich valuation multiples and a moderating pace of quarterly store expansion demand strict base support tests.
catalysts: Strong Q2 standalone revenue updates reflecting >20% YoY top-line growth
Festive demand boost across apparel and value retail formats
Board meeting scheduled for late October to approve full audited earnings
risks: Slower sequential store openings in tier-2/tier-3 cities
Compressed discretionary spending margins from promotional discounting

sectors.name: Aerospace & Defence
sectors.reason: The sector has slipped into intermediate corrective phases below 50-DMA/100-DMA levels due to institutional de-risking and supply overhangs, despite sustained MoD contract flow.
catalysts: Fresh radar and counter-drone contract awards from the Ministry of Defence
Milestone aircraft deliveries and engine manufacturing capacity expansion
Large export order pipelines for naval and commercial shipbuilding
risks: OFS equity dilution overhang in key shipbuilding PSUs
Stretched delivery cycles and component supply chain bottlenecks
Broader institutional profit taking across high-multiple PSU defense counters

news.headline: Defence Ministry Inks ₹770 Crore Deal with BEL for Anti-Drone Radar Systems; Q2 Results Set for Oct 30
news.summary: The Ministry of Defence signed a ₹770 crore contract on October 21 with Bharat Electronics Limited to procure Improved Low Level Light Weight Radars (LLLR-I) for the Indian Army to counter drone threats. This adds to the ₹533 crore order inflow disclosed earlier this month. Furthermore, the company has formally scheduled its Board of Directors meeting on October 30, 2026, to approve Q2 FY27 earnings.
news.impact: Contract accretion reinforces earnings visibility, setting up swing support checks near ₹365–₹370 ahead of the October 30 results catalyst.

news.headline: Nifty 50 Reverses From Intraday Highs to Close at 22,811 as Cyclicals Drag
news.summary: The Nifty 50 surrendered an early morning advance on October 21, falling from highs near 23,106 to settle at 22,811.35 (-0.34%). Heavy declines in engineering services and capital goods (-4.3%) and broad defensive rotation weighed on sentiment, offsetting gains across IT names. Technicians highlight 22,800 as crucial near-term swing support, with major resistance pegged at 23,200–23,300.
news.impact: Daily rejection candle below 23,000 indicates market-wide breakout attempts remain prone to failure; swing traders should tighten stops and reduce position sizing on non-earnings setups.

news.headline: Cochin Shipyard Slips Over 5% to 52-Week Lows Amid OFS Liquidity Overhang
news.summary: Shares of Cochin Shipyard broke below intermediate supports on October 21 to touch intraday lows of ₹1,160.15, extending a 3-session slump. The persistent selling pressure follows the recent 5% government stake sale via OFS, which has temporarily overshadowed positive fundamental catalysts including international orders for >40 vessels and a ₹100–250 crore river cruise ship contract.
news.impact: Breakdown below major moving averages violates multi-week swing bases; avoids fresh momentum entries until base-building and high-volume accumulation are established.

news.headline: CG Power Pulls Back 3% Into Key Support Ahead of Q2 FY27 Earnings on October 23
news.summary: CG Power and Industrial Solutions experienced a 3.01% intraday retreat to ₹825 on October 21 as electrical equipment stocks took a breather amid broader market profit booking. The company’s Board of Directors is scheduled to meet on October 23, 2026, to review and approve Q2 FY27 financial results. The market remains focused on order book execution in power systems and updates on its Sanand OSAT semiconductor joint venture.
news.impact: Pre-earnings pullback brings price into horizontal swing support near ₹820–₹830; confirmation of an earnings reaction is needed before initiating fresh base breakout trades.

news.headline: HAL Delivers First 3 Indigenous HTT-40 Trainers to IAF Under ₹6,828 Crore Deal
news.summary: Hindustan Aeronautics Limited has delivered the first three indigenous HTT-40 basic trainer aircraft to the Indian Air Force under a 70-aircraft contract valued at ₹6,828.36 crore. Deliveries mark a key execution milestone, with aircraft stationed at the Flying Instructors' School in Tambaram for instructor qualification. This follows HAL's capex push to expand AL-31FP engine assembly to 50 engines per year at Koraput.
news.impact: Execution milestone provides structural backing against sectoral selling pressure, with traders watching for a base stabilization above ₹4,650.

news.headline: Harish Bhat Exits Trent Board Ahead of Scheduled Q2 Results on October 29
news.summary: Trent Ltd announced that non-executive director Harish Bhat stepped down from the board on October 20 citing personal and professional commitments. The transition precedes the scheduled board meeting on October 29, 2026, where the company will declare audited Q2 FY27 earnings. In its preliminary operational update, Trent posted a 23% YoY rise in standalone merchandise revenue to ₹5,788 crore as the Zudio footprint crossed 1,000 stores.
news.impact: Stock is consolidating near its 20-day EMA following the early Q2 update rally; traders eye a cup-like handle pattern completion into the October 29 event.

news.headline: LTTS Surges Up To 15% on Q2 FY27 Beat, Robust AI Deal Wins, and ₹20 Dividend
news.summary: L&T Technology Services reported Q2 FY27 revenue of ₹3,040.4 crore (+12.1% YoY, +2.7% QoQ CC) with EBIT margins expanding 60 bps QoQ to 16.3%, beating consensus estimates. Net income surged 66.8% YoY to ₹548.2 crore (including a ₹165 crore gain from the SWC business divestment). The company secured >$200 million in large deal TCV (over 50% AI-related) and declared an interim dividend of ₹20 per share (record date October 27, 2026).
news.impact: High-volume gap-up breakout above multimonth resistance signals aggressive accumulation, favoring continuation pullbacks above ₹3,850.

news.headline: Jio Platforms ₹30,213 Crore Mega IPO Sees 85% Subscription in Minutes; RIL Gains
news.summary: Reliance Industries shares saw active buying as India's landmark ₹30,213-crore initial public offering of Jio Platforms opened for subscription on October 21, achieving an 85% subscription rate within the first hour of bidding. The market responded positively to the long-anticipated unlocking of value from RIL’s telecom and digital services ecosystem.
news.impact: Strong retail and institutional demand for the subsidiary listing provides a supportive floor for RIL, which is testing a breakout from a 3-week base.

news.headline: Bajaj Finance Dips 3.4% Despite Q2 Profit Jump to ₹6,367 Crore on Margin Queries
news.summary: Bajaj Finance reported a 29% YoY increase in consolidated net profit to ₹6,367 crore for Q2 FY27, with net interest income rising 24% and customer franchise expanding 16% YoY to 128.85 million. However, the stock dropped 3.4% during Wednesday's trade as the Street digested slight compression in net interest margins and elevated credit costs in specific consumer loan buckets.
news.impact: Selloff following headline numbers signals an earnings exhaustion gap; expect the stock to re-test primary support around the ₹940–₹950 band before forming a new base.

news.headline: HCL Tech Consolidates Highs After Q2 Net Profit Climbs 21% to ₹5,132 Crore
news.summary: HCL Technologies held firm near recent multi-month peaks following its Q2 FY27 earnings release, where net profit rose 21% YoY to ₹5,132 crore on 12% revenue growth to ₹35,620 crore. New deal wins totaled $3.26 billion, prompting management to maintain full-year EBIT margin guidance at 17.5%–18.5% and CC revenue growth at 2.5%–4%.
news.impact: Consistent execution and resilient guidance keep HCL Tech constructive in a high-tight consolidation flag, outperforming the benchmark index.
